title: The inspector finds, the gate certifies
owner: cairn (cairn/tools/base is the base gate class's address; CC builds)
intention: The inspector does every check and outputs only findings; the gate consumes those findings and outputs a certificate, one file type nothing else can write, signed to say the right gate code wrote it at this date and time over these hashed findings; entry gates only kick back.
why: Akien 2026-10-27, outline 19.14.1-19.14.4 (CairnCommons 3a3355ea): 'the inspector does all the checks. so there is no need for more checks. the idea was make one file type you can't write. then add a cyptographic or similar way to say that the right code wrote the certificate on this date at this time with these hashed findings. that's a thing that should be in the base gate class. the reason for entry gates was just so we could kick things back that didn't meet the entry requirements. nothing in there about who writes what.' / 'the inspectors output is consumed by the gate. the gate's output is the certificate.' / 'the inspector outputs only the findings.' / 'this was how i meant it all along.' Measured 2026-10-27: test_inspector_nexus is red because the inspector imports transitions for its grammar and transitions.emit now posts to the bus (32f500e517d7); his answer to open-495f7be4789b is that the inspector stops reaching emit.
traces_to: Akien 2026-10-27, outline 19.14.1: 'the inspector does all the checks, so there is no need for more checks' / 'the inspectors output is consumed by the gate. the gate's output is the certificate' / 'this was how i meant it all along'. Law 4 (a certificate you cannot forge is physics; who-writes-what policing is policy). Law 8 (proof before trust between peers). Law 1 (checks stated once, in the inspector). RULE 1 (the inspector's public output is findings).
how: Signing lives in the base gate class (cairn/tools/base/gate_class.py TransitionGate): on a verdict it writes a certificate carrying the hashed findings, the time, and the identity of the gate code that wrote it, signed so a hand-written or altered certificate fails verification. The check lanes now written inside cairn/tools/base/transitions.py move to inspector sieves, so the gates only compare findings and certify. The inspector stops importing the crossing machinery and reads workflow strings through a module that imports nothing heavy, which removes the socket path that reds test_inspector_nexus. The crossing itself (cursor move and journal) is recorded on the strength of a certificate; who owns it is outline Q#61. Deconstructed into children at /sorted.
falsifier: Done when: every gate's output is a certificate the base gate class writes and verifies, and a certificate written or edited by hand fails verification; the only checks are inspector sieves, and an entry gate does nothing but compare findings and kick back; the inspector imports nothing that can post, record a crossing, or reach a host, and test_inspector_nexus is green; every crossing past an entry gate names the certificate it stands on. Wrong intent if 'one file type you can't write' means something other than a signed file that is verified on read, or if Akien wants the crossing to belong to the gate.
watchme: none, because the outcome is measured by cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_inspector_nexus.py going green and by the four children reaching PROVED, each child carrying its own watch; a probe on the parent would watch what the children already prove
children: 1. The base gate class signs: cairn/tools/base/gate_class.py writes a certificate (hashed findings, date and time, identity and hash of the gate code) and verifies one on read; a hand-written or edited certificate fails. Waits on open-6dbeb274245e.
2. The checks move to the inspector: every check lane now in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py becomes a build_inspector sieve, and the entry gates only compare findings and kick back.

3. The inspector reads workflow strings through a light grammar module: parse_workflow, is_terminal, MalformedWorkflow and verify_crossing_fingerprint move to a module that imports nothing heavy, transitions re-exports them, and test_inspector_nexus goes green.
4. The crossing stands on a certificate: a forward crossing past an entry gate names the certificate it stands on, recorded by the crossing's owner. Waits on open-f17382e51f4f.

decisions.text: D1 (the /sorted builder_check): A Haiku builder would ask: what file format is a certificate, where is it written, what is signed, with what key, and who may verify it; which lanes move and to which sieves; which module holds the grammar; and what the crossing reads. This parent answers the shape and assigns each question to a child. Key custody and the crossing's owner wait on Akien (open-6dbeb274245e, open-f17382e51f4f). Each child is cast with its own decisions and rehearsed before BUILDME, so no builder builds from this parent.
